stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with lower pricing
stories.rationale: Major frontier model release with concrete pricing and coding/agent capability gains, core reader interest.
stories.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with improved coding, computer use, and efficiency across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API, with 6.2 Astra priced at $8/MTok input and $40/MTok output (80% of its predecessor). Early testers report mixed impressions of Astra, while Sol is positioned as the main workhorse model.

stories.title: OpenAI details Codex agent workflows, sandboxing, and research acceleration
stories.rationale: Directly matches agentic dev tooling and SDLC automation interest with concrete internal deployment detail.
stories.summary: OpenAI published analyses of how coding agents accelerate AI research along a 'jagged frontier,' plus internal case studies like the Codex-powered Performance Factory and technical detail on the Codex sandbox's filesystem and network controls. Related Codex Security Plugin and PR scan demos show agent-driven security review workflows, alongside independent work on external sandboxes for coding agents.

stories.title: Software factories: agentic code review and SDLC automation go mainstream
stories.rationale: Concrete numbers on agentic SDLC adoption from practitioners and executives, squarely in reader's wheelhouse.
stories.summary: CodeRabbit's CEO describes shipping over 5,000 pull requests in a month and spending $250K/month on AI while arguing human code review is dead, and Linear reports over 50% of tickets written by agents en route to $100M ARR. Satya Nadella and Pragmatic Engineer coverage examine software engineering as code becomes cheap, alongside Meta's reversal of shutting down the Conductor coding harness.

stories.title: Anthropic completes largest-ever IPO, valued at ~$1.5T
stories.rationale: Major AI business milestone with concrete pricing numbers, borderline on reader's core interests.
stories.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83.00 per share and closed the offering of over 1.1 billion Class A shares including full underwriter option exercise. Secondary reporting pegs it as the largest IPO in history at a ~$1.5T valuation, with shares opening at $111.50 and closing at $97.17 on debut.

stories.title: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Neon
stories.rationale: Major model release from DeepMind with benchmark positioning, core reader interest.
stories.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini 4 Neon, positioned as a mid-tier Opus/Sol competitor scoring 61 on the Intelligence Index. The release joins the broader Gemini 4 family which includes Carbon, Hydrogen, and Neon variants with varying reasoning levels.

stories.title: Open-weight model and local-inference advances: Inkling 2 Mini, harness adapters, MoE streaming
stories.rationale: Open-weight models, harness adapters, and efficient local inference map to evals/harness and infra interests.
stories.summary: Hugging Face released Inkling 2 Mini for local setups (running in 5.4GB quantized), harness adapters to tune models to specific agent harnesses for better cost/performance, and techniques for 180B-parameter MoE inference in 32GB RAM. Additional releases include DaisyRose-27B post-training efficiency work, the Rumble-2-Flash speech model, and an OpenRouter integration for running open-weight models.

stories.title: Lean-verified Riemann Hypothesis proof, some AI-assisted
stories.rationale: AI-assisted and formal-verification math milestone with significance to evals/formal methods, though peripheral to enterprise focus.
stories.summary: A Lean-verified proof of the Riemann Hypothesis circulated widely, with reports of two independent proofs including one developed with Claude and claims extending to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. Separate commentary frames formal verification plus AI as an emerging weapon against low-quality 'slop' output.

stories.title: Inference engineering, Gemini reasoning levels, and token fraud
stories.rationale: Practical deployment engineering, model cost/reasoning tradeoffs, and a real operational threat to AI products.
stories.summary: A Pragmatic Engineer deepdive covers inference engineering choices like model/provider selection, caching, dedicated GPUs, and KV cache concerns, while the llm-gemini update highlights Gemini 4's xhigh reasoning level and its large token/cost impact. Separately, ChatPRD's founder documents a surge of token fraud abusing free trials to resell AI usage.

stories.title: Perplexity hits $1B revenue run rate; Cloudflare pivots to 'neolab'
stories.rationale: AI business momentum and infra-adjacent strategy, moderate relevance with concrete revenue figures.
stories.summary: Perplexity reportedly reached a $1B revenue run rate, up 4x in 2026, and shipped a Monitor API. Cloudflare rebranded itself a 'neolab,' building low-latency 'System One' models to make decisions and pull data in milliseconds.

stories.title: Daniel Stenberg on AI Rust rewrites versus real curl development
stories.rationale: Grounded, numbers-based counterpoint on agentic code rewrites from a primary maintainer, matches skepticism-of-hype preference.
stories.summary: curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg noted AI agents converted 185,000 lines of C into 340,000 lines of Rust while the actual curl project merged 300+ commits and ~200 bugfixes plus vulnerability fixes in three weeks. He questions whether the AI-generated clones can keep pace with ongoing human-maintained development.
